title: The Post-Settlement Settlement
description: After you agree, ask whether there is a better deal for both — and often there is.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: Once an agreement is reached, ask one more question: is there a way to make this better for both of us? Because neither side has to reopen what is already agreed, this is a low-risk search for extra value.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: The pressure to reach a deal can crowd out creative options. With the deal secured, both sides can look for improvements that were missed, without risking the agreement already on the table.

sections.title: Real-Life Examples
content: After agreeing a price, discovering a payment schedule that suits both.
Adding a small service that costs one side little and helps the other a lot.

sections.title: What It Looks Like
content: A final "is there anything we've missed?" question.
Improvements found after the main deal is settled.

sections.title: How to Use It
sections.content: Once agreement is firm, ask both sides to hunt for mutual gains. Make clear that the existing deal stands regardless.

sections.title: Red Flags
content: Using the question to reopen and unpick the deal.
A side that agreed and then tries to claw back.

sections.title: Defense Strategies
content: Confirm the deal stands before exploring improvements.
Treat genuine improvements as optional, not as reopening.

sections.title: Mistakes People Make
content: Walking away the moment agreement is reached.
Reopening the whole negotiation instead of adding to it.

sections.title: Key Lessons
content: Deals can often be improved after agreement.
Low risk, because the deal already stands.
